projects.title: TuneIt
projects.subtitle: Algorithmic Music Flow Sequencer & Energy Optimizer
projects.summary: A sequencer that orders a playlist the way a DJ would: harmonically compatible, with a deliberate energy curve across the set.
projects.problem: Playlist ordering is usually left to shuffle or to recency. Neither respects musical key or energy, so sets lurch between incompatible tracks and flatten out emotionally.
projects.objective: Order an arbitrary playlist so consecutive tracks are harmonically compatible and the overall energy follows an intentional trajectory — at a throughput that makes it interactive rather than a batch job.
projects.architecture: A TypeScript/Express REST API fronts four independent sequencing engines. Track metadata is fetched from the YouTube Data API in batches of 12, rate-limited through Bottleneck, enriched by Google Gemini, and cached in PostgreSQL via Prisma so repeat analyses cost nothing. A Next.js 16 client renders the resulting energy trajectory and previews audio in-browser.
implementation: Four algorithmic sequencing engines built on Camelot wheel harmonic matching plus regression-based energy optimisation.
Tested and refined against music-analysis datasets including MusAV and MTG-Jamendo.
Express.js/TypeScript REST API with 12-track batching and Bottleneck rate limiting across the YouTube Data and Gemini APIs.
PostgreSQL + Prisma caching layer for track analysis results.
Next.js 16 frontend with interactive energy-trajectory visualisation and in-browser audio preview.

challenges.challenge: Third-party API quotas made per-track analysis untenable at playlist scale.
challenges.resolution: Batched requests 12 at a time behind a Bottleneck limiter and cached every analysed track in PostgreSQL, so the quota cost of a playlist falls to near zero on re-analysis.

challenges.challenge: Harmonic compatibility and energy shape pull against each other — the most compatible next track is often the wrong energy.
challenges.resolution: Separated the two concerns into distinct engines and scored candidates on a weighted objective, which let the trade-off be tuned rather than hard-coded.

projects.lessons: Caching is an architecture decision, not an optimisation. Deciding where the cache lived — at the analysed-track boundary rather than the request boundary — was what made the throughput number possible at all.

projects.title: OnSight
projects.subtitle: Automated Examination & Assessment Platform
projects.summary: Turns a PDF question paper into a running, graded, audited online examination.
projects.problem: Setting up an online exam usually means re-typing an existing paper into a form builder, then trusting an ad-hoc grading script and a permissions model that was never really designed.
projects.objective: Ingest an existing PDF paper directly into a structured exam, grade submissions reliably inside enforced time windows, and make every access attempt auditable.
projects.architecture: A Node.js/Express service over MongoDB with Mongoose. Gemini's multimodal API handles PDF-to-MCQ extraction behind a JSON schema validator; a separate grading engine owns evaluation, timing enforcement and analytics; a hierarchical RBAC layer with JWT and refresh-token rotation guards every endpoint.
implementation: PDF-to-MCQ ingestion pipeline on Gemini multimodal APIs, with JSON schema validation, input sanitisation, and fallback handling for transient extraction failures.
Grading engine that evaluates submissions, enforces exam time windows, and computes question-level performance analytics.
Post-exam grace-mark recalculation across an already-graded cohort.
Hierarchical RBAC with JWT authentication and refresh-token rotation.
Endpoint rate limiting and persistent audit logging of unauthorised access attempts.

challenges.challenge: Multimodal extraction fails non-deterministically — a paper that parses cleanly once may not the next time.
challenges.resolution: Validated every extraction against a JSON schema and wrapped the call in explicit fallback handling, so a transient failure degrades to a retry path instead of a corrupt exam.

challenges.challenge: Grades sometimes have to change after the fact, without losing the original submission record.
challenges.resolution: Made grace-mark handling a recalculation pass over stored submissions rather than a mutation of stored grades, keeping the original record intact and auditable.

projects.lessons: Anything an LLM produces has to be treated as untrusted input. The schema validator and the fallback path are not defensive extras here — they are the feature that makes the pipeline usable.

projects.title: BobAI
projects.subtitle: Natural-Language Full-Stack Application Generator
projects.summary: Describe an application in plain English; get a provisioned repository with a working multi-tier app in it.
projects.problem: Code generators tend to stop at a snippet. The gap between a generated file and a repository you can actually run is where the time goes.
projects.objective: Take a natural-language specification all the way to a provisioned GitHub repository containing a coherent multi-tier application with a matching SQL schema.
projects.architecture: A Flask REST API drives a modular scaffolding engine that targets vanilla JS, React, and Node/Express tiers. Gemini generates source, which a multi-file extraction pipeline splits with regex fallbacks; Pexels supplies contextual assets and design tokens; PyGithub provisions and pushes the repository; subprocess-driven integration tests verify the result.
implementation: Flask REST API and modular scaffolding engine producing multi-tier applications across vanilla JS, React, and Node/Express, with generated SQL schemas.
Multi-file code extraction pipeline over Gemini output, with regex fallbacks for malformed responses.
Pexels API integration injecting contextual assets and design tokens into generated source.
Repository provisioning and GitHub deployment automated with PyGithub.
Subprocess-based integration tests validating API contracts, generated-file integrity, and deployment failure handling.

challenges.challenge: Model output does not reliably respect file boundaries, so a single malformed response can corrupt a whole generated project.
challenges.resolution: Built extraction as a pipeline with regex fallbacks at each stage, so degraded output still yields separable files rather than one unusable blob.

challenges.challenge: A generated repository that does not run is worse than no repository.
challenges.resolution: Added subprocess integration tests that exercise the API contracts and file integrity of the generated project — and the deployment failure path specifically.

projects.lessons: Testing the failure path mattered more than testing the happy path. Most of what made this reliable was deciding what should happen when generation goes wrong.
